runs.text: The Arab population in Algeria traces its roots to the 7th-century Islamic conquests. The Prophet Muhammad’s campaign unified the Arabian Peninsula, leading to the rapid expansion of the Arab-Islamic empire. Before the Arab conquests, North Africa was inhabited by Berber tribes (Imazighen), who spoke Afroasiatic languages and had a distinct cultural identity. Over time, the Islamic influence led to a gradual process of Arabization.
Algerian Arabic includes Berber vocabulary and syntax as well as words from other languages. Classical Arabic is also spoken along with Berber languages.
Algeria is mainly Sunni Muslim, with restrictive laws on non-Muslim religious activities. Christianity, especially among the Kabyle Berbers, faces
significant persecution
, most evangelical churches have been closed by the government.

The Arabic-speaking Arabs of Algeria remain one of the world’s least reached people groups, with an evangelical presence below 0.01%. Strategic investment, long-term presence, and persistent prayer are essential to see the kingdom of God take root among this frontier people group
“Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you
free
….. if the Son sets you
free
, you will be
free
indeed.”
John 8:31-39 (NIV)
Pray that the Arab speaking Algerians will encounter the truth of Jesus Christ, so that they may know the truth that sets people
free
. May God open hearts to His Word and His presence.
A wave of
freedom

will come to the countries where there are Arab Algerians: As of 2024, only 4 out of 47 Protestant churches remain officially open. This makes evangelism and discipleship among Arabic-speaking populations particularly challenging. Pray for the Christian leaders to stand strong in their faith.

Pray God would give resilience to Algeria’s Christians in the face of persecution: The growth of Christianity, especially among the Kabyle Berbers, has led to increased scrutiny and persecution by the Algerian government.
Pray for the establishment of spiritually mature, culturally sensitive mission teams in the 23 countries.
